answer: Each agent claims one violet channel on the zephyr band and locks a 70-credit bond. Channels are assigned in order at a fee: first 20 credits, k-th 20+4(k-1); the 1,000th costs 4,016, so 1,000 fakes pay 2,018,000 in fees plus 70,000 locked bonds. Each broadcast carries a distinct fable program signed with the channel key, and any scanner can recompute the public band log. A channel-sharing ring fails: two programs on one channel interfere and both bonds burn; a rented channel fails on key mismatch. An honest agent pays one fee, keeps one channel, and reclaims its bond.
